blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Mata Gujri1 also tried to prevail upon the Guru, And she also prohibited him from his chosen path. Why did he hand over all his power and resources, Into the hands and custody of the Khalsa Panth? (1)
lines: Then Mata Gujri1 also tried to prevail upon the Guru,
And she also prohibited him from his chosen path.
Why did he hand over all his power and resources,
Into the hands and custody of the Khalsa Panth?

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Branding the Singhs as unruly, Mata Gujri accused them of creating indiscipline, And bringing a bad name to the Guru with their acts of recklessness. She warned the Guru that those whom he called the extraordinary Khalsa Panth, They would actually desert him in a moment of crisis and adversity. (2)
lines: Branding the Singhs as unruly,
Mata Gujri accused them of creating indiscipline,
And bringing a bad name to the Guru with their acts of recklessness.
She warned the Guru that those whom he called the extraordinary Khalsa Panth,
They would actually desert him in a moment of crisis and adversity.

blocks.text: Why should he disempower and dispossess his own sons, For these unreliable offsprings of distant strangers. But without paying anyheed to the exhortations of his mother, The Guru addressed her in the following words: (3)
lines: Why should he disempower and dispossess his own sons,
For these unreliable offsprings of distant strangers.
But without paying anyheed to the exhortations of his mother,
The Guru addressed her in the following words:

blocks.text: "My dear Mata Gujri, listen to my words, You have been incited by other people. If you persist in Khalsa Panth's condemnation, It will recoil upon your family. Since you have been misled by our adversaries, I beseech you to desist from listening to slander against the Khalsa Panth." (4)
lines: "My dear Mata Gujri, listen to my words,
You have been incited by other people.
If you persist in Khalsa Panth's condemnation,
It will recoil upon your family.
Since you have been misled by our adversaries,
I beseech you to desist from listening to slander against the Khalsa Panth."

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Satguru Guru Gobind Singh addressed the Khalsa, And gave orders to the Singhs to this effect: They (the Singhs) need not be scared of any body, And could seize anything forcibly that they needed for their needs. (5)
lines: Then Satguru Guru Gobind Singh addressed the Khalsa,
And gave orders to the Singhs to this effect: They (the Singhs) need not be scared of any body,
And could seize anything forcibly that they needed for their needs.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Singhs looted and plundered many surrounding places, Including all the settlements around the town of Kamlot2 . They captured the villages in the forested area of Jhakhi Kamlot, And plundered the hilly helmets in the valley of Anandpur Sahib. (6)
lines: The Singhs looted and plundered many surrounding places,
Including all the settlements around the town of Kamlot2 .
They captured the villages in the forested area of Jhakhi Kamlot,
And plundered the hilly helmets in the valley of Anandpur Sahib.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the Hill chiefs engaged the Singhs in a battle, But the Singhs made them run away from the battlefield. Defeated and vanquished, they retreated into their homes, And the Singhs started collecting revenue from them. (7)
lines: Thereafter, the Hill chiefs engaged the Singhs in a battle,
But the Singhs made them run away from the battlefield.
Defeated and vanquished, they retreated into their homes,
And the Singhs started collecting revenue from them.

blocks.text: The Hill chief of Kahloor3 petitioned to the emperor at Delhi, Along with the chiefs of all the Hilly Principalities.
They were the rulers of twenty-two police districts, Including the seven districts of Jalandhar4 principality. (8)
lines: They were the rulers of twenty-two police districts,
Including the seven districts of Jalandhar4 principality.

blocks.text: They attacked Anandpur Sahib after their return from Delhi, But all the forces of twenty-two hill states ran away after defeat. These hill chiefs felt extremely ashamed after their defeat, And failed to deposit revenue to the Delhi emperor. (9)
lines: They attacked Anandpur Sahib after their return from Delhi,
But all the forces of twenty-two hill states ran away after defeat.
These hill chiefs felt extremely ashamed after their defeat,
And failed to deposit revenue to the Delhi emperor.

blocks.text: They appealed to the Delhi ruler for help and protection, Otherwise they would have to pay revenue to the Singhs alone. They told that the Tenth Guru had recruited a large army, And had amassed a lot of wealth through offerings. (10)
lines: They appealed to the Delhi ruler for help and protection,
Otherwise they would have to pay revenue to the Singhs alone.
They told that the Tenth Guru had recruited a large army,
And had amassed a lot of wealth through offerings.

blocks.text: He had proclaimed himself as the Guru of whole of India, And wished to decimate the Mughal rulers of India. He proclaimed himself to be the true divinely-ordained emperor, And regarded the Mughal emperor as a counterfeit ruler. (11)
lines: He had proclaimed himself as the Guru of whole of India,
And wished to decimate the Mughal rulers of India.
He proclaimed himself to be the true divinely-ordained emperor,
And regarded the Mughal emperor as a counterfeit ruler.

blocks.text: He had no scarcity of wealth, money and means, Since he was being assisted by many alchemists. When the king Bhimchand of Kahloor stated these developments, Emperor Aurangzeb at Delhi felt extremely concerned. (12)
lines: He had no scarcity of wealth, money and means,
Since he was being assisted by many alchemists.
When the king Bhimchand of Kahloor stated these developments,
Emperor Aurangzeb at Delhi felt extremely concerned.

blocks.text: Before the Khalsa forces launched an attack on the Mughals, They should nip this evil (the Khalsa Panth) in the bud. (13)
lines: Before the Khalsa forces launched an attack on the Mughals,
They should nip this evil (the Khalsa Panth) in the bud.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughal emperor of Delhi had stationed, Ten lakh Mughal troops at the Khyber Pass. He sent written orders to these stationed troops there, That they should launch an attack on the Guru's forces. (14)
lines: The Mughal emperor of Delhi had stationed,
Ten lakh Mughal troops at the Khyber Pass.
He sent written orders to these stationed troops there,
That they should launch an attack on the Guru's forces.

blocks.text: The Mughal forces immediately raided the Khalsa from all the four sides, As a sharp knife runs through a Melon so quickly. There were some Sikh soldiers among the Mughal forces, Who sent a message to Anandpur after hearing these orders. (15)
lines: The Mughal forces immediately raided the Khalsa from all the four sides,
As a sharp knife runs through a Melon so quickly.
There were some Sikh soldiers among the Mughal forces,
Who sent a message to Anandpur after hearing these orders.

blocks.text: People started deserting Anandpur after hearing this news, As they were so much panicked to find a safe shelter. Guru Gobind Singh tried his best to allay people's fears, Saying that God would surely protect and shield them. (16)
lines: People started deserting Anandpur after hearing this news,
As they were so much panicked to find a safe shelter.
Guru Gobind Singh tried his best to allay people's fears,
Saying that God would surely protect and shield them.

blocks.text: But the people started fleeing without listening to Guru's advice, As they did not accept and obey Guru's instructions.
The Guru advised them to remain determined and composed, As the Divine power would surely provide them with protection. (17)
lines: The Guru advised them to remain determined and composed,
As the Divine power would surely provide them with protection.

blocks.text: But so many rumours spread about the arrival of the Mughal forces, That no body could counter these and stop the fleeing people. The Dogras5 of twenty-two hill states attacked from one side, Even as forces of twenty-two states of Jalandhar raided from the other side. (18)
lines: But so many rumours spread about the arrival of the Mughal forces,
That no body could counter these and stop the fleeing people.
The Dogras5 of twenty-two hill states attacked from one side,
Even as forces of twenty-two states of Jalandhar raided from the other side.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Mughal forces from the garrisons of Sirhind6 and Malerkotla7 , Surrounded Anandpur Sahib from the Southern side of the city of Ropar. The troops from city of Lahore occupied Doaba8 region in the west, While the forces of the Hill chiefs covered the mountainous North-East side. (19)
lines: The Mughal forces from the garrisons of Sirhind6 and Malerkotla7 ,
Surrounded Anandpur Sahib from the Southern side of the city of Ropar.
The troops from city of Lahore occupied Doaba8 region in the west,
While the forces of the Hill chiefs covered the mountainous North-East side.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

They surrounded Anandpur Sahib from all the four sides, And blocked all supplies of rations and fodder for the animals. The people, then, had to pass through such difficult times, That they decided to flee from this dangerous area. (20)
lines: They surrounded Anandpur Sahib from all the four sides,
And blocked all supplies of rations and fodder for the animals.
The people, then, had to pass through such difficult times,
That they decided to flee from this dangerous area.

blocks.text: Then Guru Gobind Singh told the frightened populace, That they could not save their lives by deserting the place. God would certainly provide a way out of this situation, As a sudden spell of rain puts down a raging fire. (21)
lines: Then Guru Gobind Singh told the frightened populace,
That they could not save their lives by deserting the place.
God would certainly provide a way out of this situation,
As a sudden spell of rain puts down a raging fire.

blocks.text: Since the Guru had a committed army of four thousand Singhs with him, Even four lakh mercenary soldiers dared not attack them. If they were slightly aware of their status of being paid soldiers, They would never dare to attack his committed Singhs. (22)
lines: Since the Guru had a committed army of four thousand Singhs with him,
Even four lakh mercenary soldiers dared not attack them.
If they were slightly aware of their status of being paid soldiers,
They would never dare to attack his committed Singhs.

blocks.text: The frightened populace appealed to Mata Gujri, Guru's mother, That she should bring about a rapprochement with the hill chiefs. But the Guru told Mata Gujri that the hill chiefs were traitors, Who would rob and slaughter the Sikhs if they ventured out. (23)
lines: The frightened populace appealed to Mata Gujri,
Guru's mother,
That she should bring about a rapprochement with the hill chiefs.
But the Guru told Mata Gujri that the hill chiefs were traitors,
Who would rob and slaughter the Sikhs if they ventured out.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Guru told his mother that the hill chiefs had been traitors since beginning, And advised her not to trust those wily hill chiefs. They would capture all the escaping people, And put all of them behind the bars. (24)
lines: The Guru told his mother that the hill chiefs had been traitors since beginning,
And advised her not to trust those wily hill chiefs.
They would capture all the escaping people,
And put all of them behind the bars.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The mother replied when the hill chiefs were swearing an oath on their idols, How could they betray and commit a fraud on the Sikhs? The Guru said that she should test their loyalty, By sending out stray articles of refuse and garbage. (25)
lines: The mother replied when the hill chiefs were swearing an oath on their idols,
How could they betray and commit a fraud on the Sikhs?
The Guru said that she should test their loyalty,
By sending out stray articles of refuse and garbage.

blocks.text: The Guru prepared a few packages of discarded articles, For testing the promised vows and intentions of hill chiefs.
These packages were loaded on carriages and sent out, As if a great consignment of valuables was being sent out by the Guru. (26)
lines: These packages were loaded on carriages and sent out,
As if a great consignment of valuables was being sent out by the Guru.

blocks.text: As the news of this outgoing rich consignment reached the hill chiefs' ears, They immediately pounced upon the loaded carriages to rob these? The Guru exposed the treachery of the treacherous hill chiefs, Who had violated their religious oaths for trifles. (27)
lines: As the news of this outgoing rich consignment reached the hill chiefs' ears,
They immediately pounced upon the loaded carriages to rob these?
The Guru exposed the treachery of the treacherous hill chiefs,
Who had violated their religious oaths for trifles.

blocks.text: By pouncing upon garbage of worn out shoes and rags, They had humiliated themselves without getting any valuables. Even then Mata Gujri did not agree with Guru's advice, And threatened to depart from Anandpur at the next sunrise. (28)
lines: By pouncing upon garbage of worn out shoes and rags,
They had humiliated themselves without getting any valuables.
Even then Mata Gujri did not agree with Guru's advice,
And threatened to depart from Anandpur at the next sunrise.

blocks.text: Mata Gujri, being persuaded and incited by he populace, She was determined to leave Anandpur Sahib immediately. People had compelled her to declare this decision to depart, They also compelled her to lead them out of Anandpur Sahib. (29)
lines: Mata Gujri, being persuaded and incited by he populace,
She was determined to leave Anandpur Sahib immediately.
People had compelled her to declare this decision to depart,
They also compelled her to lead them out of Anandpur Sahib.

blocks.text: When this news of peoples' desertion reached the Guru, The Guru analysed the consequences of such a decision. He concluded that nobody could survive through desertion at this moment. And the world would blame his leadership for this humiliation. (30)
lines: When this news of peoples' desertion reached the Guru,
The Guru analysed the consequences of such a decision.
He concluded that nobody could survive through desertion at this moment.
And the world would blame his leadership for this humiliation.

blocks.text: What could be done when people refused to obey Guru's advice? When the people were bent upon fleeing in all the four directions? Then a thought occurred in Satguru's agitated mind, That he should take a written undertaking from these people. (31)
lines: What could be done when people refused to obey Guru's advice?
When the people were bent upon fleeing in all the four directions?
Then a thought occurred in Satguru's agitated mind,
That he should take a written undertaking from these people.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Satguru put forth this proposal before the people, That they should give this written undertaking to him. That the Guru had tried his best to make them stay put, But they, his followers, had not obeyed his orders. (32)
lines: Then Satguru put forth this proposal before the people,
That they should give this written undertaking to him.
That the Guru had tried his best to make them stay put,
But they, his followers, had not obeyed his orders.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Then the Guru asked for a second undertaking to the effect: That neither he was their Guru, nor were they his Sikhs. The people immediately gave the same written undertaking, As they had been directed to write by the Guru. (33)
lines: Then the Guru asked for a second undertaking to the effect: That neither he was their Guru, nor were they his Sikhs.
The people immediately gave the same written undertaking,
As they had been directed to write by the Guru.

blocks.text: All those who had been courtiers, servants and personal attendants, Became hostile and traitors at this moment of crisis. God had brought about such a twist in the turn of events, That the people had fallen on bad times and misfortune. (34)
lines: All those who had been courtiers, servants and personal attendants,
Became hostile and traitors at this moment of crisis.
God had brought about such a twist in the turn of events,
That the people had fallen on bad times and misfortune.

blocks.text: All the people had betrayed their faith in the Guru, Such had been the curse and wrath of the times. The more the Guru tried to pacify and assure the people, The more the people hastened to flee and desert him. (35)
lines: All the people had betrayed their faith in the Guru,
Such had been the curse and wrath of the times.
The more the Guru tried to pacify and assure the people,
The more the people hastened to flee and desert him.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Satguru turned his attention towards his initiated Singhs, In order to ask for a similar undertaking from them. But the Khalsa Panth of initiated Singhs declined to give any such undertaking, Asserting that they would neither disobey nor betray the Khalsa Panth. (36)
lines: Then Satguru turned his attention towards his initiated Singhs,
In order to ask for a similar undertaking from them.
But the Khalsa Panth of initiated Singhs declined to give any such undertaking,
Asserting that they would neither disobey nor betray the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Khalsa Singhs declared that they were the repositories of their faith, That they would not betray their faith even at the cost of their lives. That they were ready to die hundred times, what to talk of one sacrifice, That they would not betray their faith at any cost.(37)
lines: The Khalsa Singhs declared that they were the repositories of their faith,
That they would not betray their faith even at the cost of their lives.
That they were ready to die hundred times, what to talk of one sacrifice,
That they would not betray their faith at any cost.

blocks.text: That whatever task they would be assigned by the Guru, They would stick to their duty till the last breath of their lives. This assertion of vows by the Singhs endeared them to the Guru, Who, overwhelmed with their loyalty, addressed them as follows: (38)
lines: That whatever task they would be assigned by the Guru,
They would stick to their duty till the last breath of their lives.
This assertion of vows by the Singhs endeared them to the Guru,
Who, overwhelmed with their loyalty, addressed them as follows:

blocks.text: Praise be to the Khalsa and Praise be to this organization of Singhs, Who had preserved the true worth of the spirit of Sikhism. Then the Khalsa's initiated Singhs entreated the Guru, That he should assign them the most arduous task. (39)
lines: Praise be to the Khalsa and Praise be to this organization of Singhs,
Who had preserved the true worth of the spirit of Sikhism.
Then the Khalsa's initiated Singhs entreated the Guru,
That he should assign them the most arduous task.

blocks.text: Then Satguru Guru Gobind Singh told those faithful Singhs, That they would accompany him wherever he went. While the Khalsa Singhs accepted the Guru's proposal to stand by him, The general populace prepared to flee from the place. (40)
lines: Then Satguru Guru Gobind Singh told those faithful Singhs,
That they would accompany him wherever he went.
While the Khalsa Singhs accepted the Guru's proposal to stand by him,
The general populace prepared to flee from the place.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Guru Gobind Singh, taking his four sons along with him, Made preparations to depart from Anandpur Sahib. He left Anandpur Sahib at the time of dusk, And proceeded towards the city of Ropar with great care. (41)
lines: Guru Gobind Singh, taking his four sons along with him,
Made preparations to depart from Anandpur Sahib.
He left Anandpur Sahib at the time of dusk,
And proceeded towards the city of Ropar with great care.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

A battery of few Singhs who were ordered to keep the rearguard, Were among the most distinguished warriors and trusted Singhs. And an other battery of Singhs formed the front guard in the same formation, While two other squads provided a cover from the flanks. (42)
lines: A battery of few Singhs who were ordered to keep the rearguard,
Were among the most distinguished warriors and trusted Singhs.
And an other battery of Singhs formed the front guard in the same formation,
While two other squads provided a cover from the flanks.

blocks.text: All the families and their members were kept in the centre, The Guru himself stood among them to guard them. The moment the Hill chiefs' forces attacked from the back, They were repulsed and beaten by the rearguard Singhs. (43)
lines: All the families and their members were kept in the centre,
The Guru himself stood among them to guard them.
The moment the Hill chiefs' forces attacked from the back,
They were repulsed and beaten by the rearguard Singhs.

blocks.text: As the Sirsa9 rivulet was also in torrential flood ahead, There was calamity staring them in the face from both sides. This two-sided calamitous situation disheartened the people, Who scattered and scampered in several directions. (44)
lines: As the Sirsa9 rivulet was also in torrential flood ahead,
There was calamity staring them in the face from both sides.
This two-sided calamitous situation disheartened the people,
Who scattered and scampered in several directions.

blocks.text: Those who ventured to return towards Anandpur Sahib, They were robbed and plundered by Hill chiefs' forces. Those who ventured to jump into the flooded rivulet, They were carried away by the strong current to unknown places. (45)
lines: Those who ventured to return towards Anandpur Sahib,
They were robbed and plundered by Hill chiefs' forces.
Those who ventured to jump into the flooded rivulet,
They were carried away by the strong current to unknown places.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Some efforts were made to cross the river at dawn, When the water level in the stream came slightly down, People jumped into the river at different intervals, Without waiting for any assistance from any one else. (46)
lines: Some efforts were made to cross the river at dawn,
When the water level in the stream came slightly down,
People jumped into the river at different intervals,
Without waiting for any assistance from any one else.

blocks.text: Only two elder sons of Guru Gobind Singh, Could manage to keep company with the Guru. The two younger sons were left in the company of the grandmother, As circumstances had brought about such a dispensation. (47)
lines: Only two elder sons of Guru Gobind Singh,
Could manage to keep company with the Guru.
The two younger sons were left in the company of the grandmother,
As circumstances had brought about such a dispensation.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

This was a moment of great crisis and extreme adversity for everyone, That every one got scattered and separated from each other. It was as momentous and trying a time for everyone, As had struck Sri Krishna during his escape from the battlefield. (48)
lines: This was a moment of great crisis and extreme adversity for everyone,
That every one got scattered and separated from each other.
It was as momentous and trying a time for everyone,
As had struck Sri Krishna during his escape from the battlefield.

blocks.text: When Lord Krishan, defeated by Kalyavan, ran away from the field, He had taken refuge behind the body of sleeping Muchkund10. Similarly, when the people came under a severe attack of the Hill chiefs, They were brutally attacked from all the four sides. (49)
lines: When Lord Krishan, defeated by Kalyavan, ran away from the field,
He had taken refuge behind the body of sleeping Muchkund10.
Similarly, when the people came under a severe attack of the Hill chiefs,
They were brutally attacked from all the four sides.

blocks.text: Since the moisture had entered into all the ammunition and the muskets, These became unserviceable for firing shots at the enemy. Everyone lost his or her shoes in the strong current, Such a calamity struck everyone during this moment of crisis. (50)
lines: Since the moisture had entered into all the ammunition and the muskets,
These became unserviceable for firing shots at the enemy.
Everyone lost his or her shoes in the strong current,
Such a calamity struck everyone during this moment of crisis.

blocks.text: Whatever little could be retrieved during this ordeal, Was drowned in the strongly flooded rivulet. Soon they were confronted by the Muslim forces of Ropar, Whose many brave Pathan soldiers were killed by the Guru's Singhs. (51)
lines: Whatever little could be retrieved during this ordeal,
Was drowned in the strongly flooded rivulet.
Soon they were confronted by the Muslim forces of Ropar,
Whose many brave Pathan soldiers were killed by the Guru's Singhs.

blocks.text: Earlier, many of them had been the paid servants at the Guru's court, Who had received innumerable awards from the Guru. Those who had been rewarded with robes and horses by the Guru, Had turned traitors and failed to serve the Guru. (52)
lines: Earlier, many of them had been the paid servants at the Guru's court,
Who had received innumerable awards from the Guru.
Those who had been rewarded with robes and horses by the Guru,
Had turned traitors and failed to serve the Guru.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Satguru used to love and admire those Pathans, And always rewarded them with expensive robes of honour. Hoping that they would fight against the hill chiefs along with him, The Guru used to assist them financially and in kind. (53)
lines: Satguru used to love and admire those Pathans,
And always rewarded them with expensive robes of honour.
Hoping that they would fight against the hill chiefs along with him,
The Guru used to assist them financially and in kind.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Satguru approached them at their home town of Ropar, But they turned hostile when he called at them. The Pathans had got constructed a big fortified Mansion for residence, Which the Guru wished to occupy for an ecounter with his enemies. (54)
lines: Satguru approached them at their home town of Ropar,
But they turned hostile when he called at them.
The Pathans had got constructed a big fortified Mansion for residence,
Which the Guru wished to occupy for an ecounter with his enemies.

blocks.text: The Pathans refused the entry to the Guru by closing their doors, For which he cursed their Mansion to be eroded by the river. When all the Lodhi" Pathans of Ropar betrayed the Guru's trust, He cursed them to be ruined along with their mansions. (55)
lines: The Pathans refused the entry to the Guru by closing their doors,
For which he cursed their Mansion to be eroded by the river.
When all the Lodhi" Pathans of Ropar betrayed the Guru's trust,
He cursed them to be ruined along with their mansions.

blocks.text: The Guru marched towards the place known as Kotla12 , Whose residents opened their doors for Guru's shelter. But the Guru did not like the proffered building, As it was not found suitable for a military encounter with the enemy. (56)
lines: The Guru marched towards the place known as Kotla12 ,
Whose residents opened their doors for Guru's shelter.
But the Guru did not like the proffered building,
As it was not found suitable for a military encounter with the enemy.

blocks.text: Then Satguru surveyed the region ahead of this place, And glanced upon a big building upon a hillock. He immediately marched towards this raised structure, And took shelter in this big Mansion upon a hillock. (57)
lines: Then Satguru surveyed the region ahead of this place,
And glanced upon a big building upon a hillock.
He immediately marched towards this raised structure,
And took shelter in this big Mansion upon a hillock.
